facts.text: Leoma hosts the Lawrence County Genealogical Society, a non‑profit founded in 1983 that preserves local family histories and historic documents.
The society’s archives include vital records, cemetery lists, and newspaper clippings that researchers can access for free online whenever possible.
Leoma’s public library offers a Local History page and a TNGenWeb portal that provide transcriptions of county sources and articles on local history.
The town sits just south of Lawrenceburg along Route 43, a historic corridor that once carried early settlers between Loretto and Lawrenceburg.
Wilburn Grist Mill, a preserved 19th‑century water‑powered mill, still stands in Leoma and is a reminder of the town’s agricultural past.
Leoma’s archives hold microfilm copies of deeds up to 1998 and trust deeds up to 1992, allowing genealogists to trace property ownership across generations.
